What we do  ·  Applied AI & Data The AI decides. Who answers for it?

We build AI into the processes that carry real cost and real risk. Each system gets the level of autonomy its controls can support, with a named person accountable at every gate, meaning every point where a person must approve.

6–16 WEEKSA WORKING SYSTEM, NOT A PILOTBUILT BY US · REVIEWED INDEPENDENTLY
Why this pillar exists

Most programs do not fail on the model.

They fail on the distance between what the system was allowed to do and what anybody had built the controls to survive. That distance is measurable, and it is the thing we manage.

01

Autonomy outruns the controls

A system reaches the rung where it acts on its own months before anybody writes the limits, the log or the stop. Nothing goes wrong until it does, all at once.

02

Nobody is accountable at the gate

There is an approval step, but no one whose job is to decline. An approval that cannot be refused is a button.

03

The data was never the strong part

The model is scrutinized for months. The data extract it stands on has often not been reconciled since it was built.

The ladder

Five rungs. Each one is earned, not assumed.

Autonomy works like a ladder. Each rung is a level of independence, and each one needs a named control in place before the system stands on it. Choose a rung.

AUTONOMY— OF 5 RUNGS EARNED
Select a rung

Five levels of autonomy. Each one is a different system with different consequences, and each one has a control that has to exist before you stand on it.

Most programs fail because a system was placed on rung four while the controls of rung two were still being written. Applied AI & Data exists to keep those two things in step.

The boundary

We build it. An independent reviewer signs it off.

Three steps. We build and later remediate. The opinion in between comes from a reviewer outside the build team.

STEP 01 · ORVIX

We build and run it

Design, integration and operation of the system, with a named person accountable at every gate that matters. This is delivery work, handed over with a runbook.

STEP 02 · INDEPENDENT REVIEWER

An independent reviewer forms the opinion

The assurance opinion on anything we built comes from outside the team that built it. When it must carry weight externally, an independent party gives it.

STEP 03 · ORVIX

We fix what the review found

We fix what the independent review identifies, and the same reviewer checks the fix.

We ask other vendors to keep building and assuring apart. We hold our own work to the same standard.

Questions we are asked

Before you ask us.

Does Orvix build, or advise?
In this pillar, builds. This is delivery work with a named duty owner and an operational handover. Independence is kept a different way: the assurance opinion on anything we built comes from an independent party.
Who gives the assurance opinion on what you build?
An independent party outside our build team. We tell clients that no organization should audit its own estate, and we apply that to ourselves. Regulators also give far more weight to an opinion that does not come from the builder.
Can you work on top of a model we already have?
Yes, and often that is the right answer. The rung the system is standing on matters far more than which model is underneath it.

Start with the rung, not the model.

Tell us what the system is allowed to do without asking. Within thirty minutes we will tell you which controls that rung requires.
